name: 2-Row Pale Malt
description: Clean, versatile workhorse base malt for American craft styles. Provides clean, mild malt sweetness with neutral grain character and very high diastatic power capable of converting high proportions of unmalted adjuncts.
typicalUsage: Foundation grain for American IPAs, Pale Ales, Lagers, and Stouts. Provides reliable extract yield and high enzymatic conversion.

name: 6-Row Pale Malt
description: Traditional American barley malt with thick husks and exceptionally high protein and enzyme content. Imparts a more grainy, husky flavor than 2-row and possesses massive diastatic power for converting corn and rice adjuncts.
typicalUsage: Historic American lagers, cream ales, and pre-prohibition styles using 20–40% corn or rice adjuncts.

name: Pilsner Malt
description: The palest base malt available, gently kilned to preserve delicate malt aroma and high enzyme activity. Imparts clean, refreshing, sweet bread dough and fresh cracker notes without color contribution.
typicalUsage: Standard base malt for continental lagers, Pilsners, Belgian ales, and delicate golden styles.

name: Barke Pilsner Malt
description: Heritage Bavarian 2-row summer barley cultivar prized by Franconian brewers for intense malty aroma, full body, head retention, and pristine lautering properties.
typicalUsage: Premium Bavarian and Bohemian lagers where an authentic deep bready backbone is desired without darkening.

name: Vienna Malt
description: Kilned slightly higher than Pilsner malt to develop rich golden-amber hues, soft bread crust character, and elegant toasty sweetness. Self-converting base malt that rounds out malt complexity.
typicalUsage: Base or major grist contributor (20–100%) for Vienna Lagers, Märzen, Festbier, and amber ales.

name: Munich Malt (Light / Type I)
description: Cured at elevated moisture and kilned higher to generate prominent melanoidins. Imparts rich, bready, malty depth, a luscious orange-amber color, and distinctive Bavarian malt character.
typicalUsage: Core grist for Dunkel, Märzen, Doppelbock, and Bocks; used in smaller percentages (5–20%) to add depth to IPAs and pale ales.

name: Munich Malt (Dark / Type II)
description: Kilned more intensely than Type I, developing deep golden-brown colors, heavy crusty breadiness, and pronounced toffee-like melanoidin richness while still retaining self-converting enzymatic strength.
typicalUsage: Up to 100% of grist in Munich Dunkel and Doppelbock; accent malt in porters, stouts, and dark lagers.

name: Maris Otter Pale Ale Malt
description: The quintessential British heritage 2-row winter barley variety bred in Cambridge in 1966. Renowned globally for its deep, rich, bready, and distinctly nutty malt profile and superb brewhouse reliability.
typicalUsage: The gold-standard base malt for British Bitters, English IPAs, Stouts, Porters, and Barleywines.

name: Golden Promise Pale Ale Malt
description: Traditional Scottish 2-row semi-dwarf spring barley cultivar yielding a soft, sweet, clean, slightly bready profile without cloying sweetness. Famous as the base for Scotch Ales and prized by modern hazy IPA brewers.
typicalUsage: Base malt for Scottish Ales, Wee Heavies, British Bitters, and juicy/hazy IPAs.

name: Pale Ale Malt (British / Domestic)
description: Kilned slightly darker and longer than standard 2-row pale malt to mute grassy raw grain flavors and accentuate bready biscuit sweetness.
typicalUsage: Base malt for English and American pale ales, IPAs, bitters, and amber ales.

name: Biscuit Malt
description: Uniquely kilned Belgian specialty malt producing warm, roasted aroma and dry, savory warm-bread and toasted biscuit flavors without caramel sweetness.
typicalUsage: 5–15% of grist to impart crisp, warm biscuit notes and golden-amber tint in Belgian ales, bitters, and amber lagers.

name: Victory Malt
description: Lightly roasted American specialty malt characterized by distinctive toasted biscuit, baking bread, and nutty roasted peanut aroma without dark roast bitterness.
typicalUsage: 3–15% in American Browns, Ambers, Porters, and Nut Browns for toasted nut complexity and copper color.

name: Amber Malt
description: Historic British kilned malt toasted intensely on dry kiln floors. Delivers assertive, crisp, dry toasty biscuit and pie crust flavors with subtle coffee and woody undertones.
typicalUsage: 5–15% in English Porters, Milds, Bitters, and historic London Ales for authentic dry toast crunch.

name: Brown Malt
description: The historic heart of 18th-century London Porter. Hard-kilned over hardwood fires in antiquity, modern versions provide intense toasty, woody, dry espresso and bitter chocolate nuances without astringency.
typicalUsage: 5–15% in English Porters, Baltic Porters, Brown Ales, and historic recreations.

name: Aromatic Malt
description: High-kilned Belgian malt with pronounced malt aroma and intense deep bread crust flavor. Imparts vibrant amber to reddish hues and robust malt backbone.
typicalUsage: 5–20% in Belgian Dubbels, Tripels, Bière de Garde, and dark abbey ales.

name: Melanoidin Malt
description: Specialty malt produced with controlled stewing and kilning to concentrate flavor-active melanoidin compounds. Simulates the deep, rounded malt complexity of traditional multi-step decoction mashing.
typicalUsage: 5–15% in German lagers, Bocks, and Scottish Ales to simulate decoction mash character.

name: Carapils / Dextrin Malt
description: Very lightly stewed crystal malt containing glassy, unfermentable dextrins. Significantly enhances head retention, foam stability, and body without contributing flavor, aroma, or color.
typicalUsage: 3–10% in light lagers, pale ales, and IPAs for foam stability and fuller mouthfeel.

name: Caramel / Crystal 20L
description: Light caramel malt providing a gentle golden-amber hue, sweet honey, mild caramel, and slight candy sweetness with unfermentable body builders.
typicalUsage: 5–10% in Blonde Ales, Light Bitters, Pale Ales, and Session IPAs.

name: Caramel / Crystal 40L
description: Medium-light caramel malt delivering rich golden-copper color, sweet toffee, soft toasted marshmallow, and light toasted nut complexity.
typicalUsage: 5–15% in American Pale Ales, Ambers, IPAs, and English Bitters.

name: Caramel / Crystal 60L
description: The quintessential mid-range caramel malt. Imparts deep amber-red color, robust rich toffee, toasted caramel, and subtle raisin sweetness.
typicalUsage: 5–15% in American Amber Ales, Red Ales, IPAs, Porters, and Strong Bitters.

name: Caramel / Crystal 80L
description: Dark caramel malt imparting deep red to dark copper color, burnt sugar, dark toffee, and pronounced raisin and dried plum fruitiness.
typicalUsage: 3–10% in Dark Ales, Porters, Stouts, Barleywines, and Scottish Wee Heavies.

name: Caramel / Crystal 120L
description: Very dark crystal malt characterized by deep reddish-brown color, intense bittersweet burnt sugar, bitter toffee, prune, and dark fruit complexity.
typicalUsage: 3–10% in Imperial Stouts, Baltic Porters, Old Ales, and Barleywines.

name: Special B Malt
description: Iconic, deeply stewed and double-roasted Belgian crystal malt. Legendary for imparting profound dark stone fruit, raisin, prune, plum, and dark brown sugar richness without roasted astringency.
typicalUsage: 3–10% in Belgian Dubbels, Dark Strong Ales, Quadrupels, and winter warmers.

name: Caramunich II
description: Drum-roasted German caramel malt made from Bavarian 2-row barley. Delivers intense malt sweetness, dark amber to copper tones, and biscuit-caramel complexity.
typicalUsage: 5–10% in Märzen, Bocks, Dunkel, and Belgian ales.

name: Chocolate Malt
description: Roasted slowly in specialized roasting drums. Imparts rich dark chocolate, bittersweet cocoa, roasted espresso, and deep brown to mahogany hues without harsh acrid bitterness.
typicalUsage: 3–10% in English Porters, American Stouts, Brown Ales, and Black IPAs.

name: Pale Chocolate Malt
description: Roasted gently to an intermediate dark brown color. Legendary for producing smooth milk chocolate, roasted hazelnut, and mellow mocha notes with none of the harshness of darker grains.
typicalUsage: 3–10% in Milds, Porters, Brown Ales, and Session Stouts.

name: Roasted Barley (Unmalted)
description: Unmalted raw barley roasted to extreme temperatures. Imparts the defining dry, assertive, bittersweet espresso, charcoal, and coffee roast characteristic of authentic Irish Dry Stouts. Aids dense foam stability.
typicalUsage: 5–10% in Irish Dry Stouts, Export Stouts, and Imperial Stouts.

name: Black Patent Malt
description: Heavily roasted malt invented in 1817 by Daniel Wheeler. Provides jet black color, sharp dry roasty bitterness, and intense charcoal/smoky nuances.
typicalUsage: 1–5% for deep black color adjustment in Porters and Stouts; used sparingly.

name: Carafa Special III (De-husked)
description: Carefully de-husked dark roasted malt from Weyermann. Delivers rich, pitch-black color, subtle coffee aroma, and dark beer body with almost none of the harsh astringency or acrid bitterness of husked grains.
typicalUsage: 1–5% in German Schwarzbier, Baltic Porters, Black IPAs, and Dunkel for black color with smooth drinkability.

name: Midnight Wheat Malt
description: Huskless roasted wheat malt from Briess. Because wheat lacks an outer husk, it can be roasted to extreme darkness without releasing harsh phenolic tannins or bitter bite.
typicalUsage: 1–5% for deep black color in Black IPAs, Schwarzbiers, Porters, and smooth dark ales.

name: Flaked Oats
description: Pre-gelatinized rolled oat flakes rich in beta-glucans, lipids, and soluble proteins. Imparts a luxurious, silky-smooth creaminess, full velvety mouthfeel, and stable persistent haze.
typicalUsage: 10–30% in Oatmeal Stouts, Hazy/New England IPAs, and Belgian Witbiers.

name: Pale Wheat Malt
description: Malted wheat kernel lacking an outer husk. Features very high protein content contributing thick rocky meringue-like foam, soft doughy mouthfeel, and tart crisp graininess.
typicalUsage: 50–70% in German Weissbier; 5–20% in American ales and lagers for head retention.

name: Malted Rye
description: Malted rye grains containing high levels of beta-glucans. Contributes a distinctive dry, spicy, peppery, pumpernickel-bread crispness and rich viscous body.
typicalUsage: 10–30% in Rye IPAs, Roggenbier, and Farmhouse ales.

name: Flaked Barley
description: Unmalted rolled barley providing unfermentable proteins and glucans that build exceptional head retention and a creamy, dry graininess characteristic of Irish stouts.
typicalUsage: 5–20% in Dry Stouts, Porters, and Milds for foam stability and body.

name: Flaked Corn (Maize)
description: Pre-gelatinized flaked maize grain. Imparts high fermentable sugar content to lighten beer body, decrease malt haze, and add a subtle sweet corn sweetness.
typicalUsage: 10–40% in American Lagers, Cream Ales, and Pre-Prohibition styles.

name: Flaked Rice
description: Pre-gelatinized rolled rice flakes yielding the absolute cleanest, driest, most neutral fermentable sugar source. Lightens beer body and color with zero residual grain sweetness.
typicalUsage: 10–40% in Japanese Dry Lagers, American Light Lagers, and Brut IPAs.

name: Acidulated Malt (Sauermalz)
description: Pilsner malt naturally fermented with lactic acid bacteria (*Lactobacillus*) to 1–2% natural lactic acid. Traditionally used in Germany to lower mash pH in compliance with the Reinheitsgebot.
typicalUsage: 1–5% for mash pH adjustment; 5–10% in Gose and Berliner Weisse for tart acidity.

name: Smoked Malt (Rauchmalt)
description: Pilsner-grade barley malt dried over flaming cured beechwood logs in Bamberg kilns. Infuses a rich, savory, campfire, bacon, and wood-smoke aroma while retaining full diastatic conversion power.
typicalUsage: Up to 100% in Bamberg Rauchbier, smoked porters, and specialty lagers.

name: Floor-Malted Bohemian Pilsner
description: Traditional Moravian 2-row barley steeped and germinated on cool stone floors in the traditional Bohemian method. Imparts unmatched rich maltiness, honeyed bread, and authentic Czech lager character.
typicalUsage: Single base malt for Czech Premium Pale Lager (Bohemian Pilsner) and Czech dark and amber lagers.

name: Halcyon Pale Ale Malt
description: Traditional British 2-row winter barley cultivar, bred from Maris Otter. Imparts a bright, clean, crisp biscuity flavor slightly drier than Maris Otter.
typicalUsage: Base malt for English Pale Ales, IPAs, Bitters, and Golden Ales.

name: Best Red X Malt
description: Proprietary specialty German malt kilned to produce a brilliant, luminous fiery red beer color when brewed up to 100% of the grist, without requiring crystal or roasted malts.
typicalUsage: Up to 100% of grist for Irish Red Ales, Red IPAs, Amber Ales, and Märzen for fiery ruby hues.

name: Abbey Malt
description: Deeply kilned European specialty malt imparting intense cooked bread crust, biscuit, and rich dark fruit nuances along with a deep warm copper tone.
typicalUsage: 5–25% in Belgian Dubbels, Trappist ales, and strong abbey beers.

name: Special Roast Malt
description: Drum-roasted American specialty malt providing complex warm sourdough, toasted bran, and tangy deep biscuit flavors with a deep red-orange color.
typicalUsage: 3–10% in Nut Browns, Amber Ales, Porters, and ESBs for sourdough complexity.

name: Honey Malt (Gambrinus)
description: Unique European-style brumalt produced by Gambrinus Malting in British Columbia. Imparts an intense, natural floral wildflower honey sweetness and rich golden hue.
typicalUsage: 2–8% in Blonde Ales, IPAs, and Wheat beers for distinct honey sweetness.

name: Carafoam Malt
description: Drum-cooked German dextrin malt designed specifically to enhance beer foam volume, lace stability, and body without contributing sweetness or color.
typicalUsage: 5–15% in German Pilsners, Helles, and Festbiers for dense, rocky foam.

name: Caraamber Malt
description: Drum-roasted German caramel malt imparting glowing red and amber hues, soft toffee, warm biscuit, and rounded malt body.
typicalUsage: 5–15% in Red Ales, Bocks, and Amber Lagers.

name: Carared Malt
description: German caramel malt specifically engineered to promote a vibrant ruby-red shine in beer while providing soft honey, cereal, and caramel notes.
typicalUsage: 5–20% in Red Ales, Altbier, and Scottish Ales.

name: Caravienne Malt
description: Light Belgian crystal malt with high levels of unfermentable sugars. Provides golden hues, warm caramel, toffee sweetness, and rich bready fullness.
typicalUsage: 5–15% in Belgian Blondes, Tripels, Saison, and Abbey ales.

name: Carafa Special I (De-husked)
description: Lightest de-husked roasted malt from Weyermann. Delivers rich dark brown color, smooth coffee notes, and milk chocolate without sharp astringency.
typicalUsage: 1–5% in Dunkel, Altbier, and Milds for dark color with gentle finish.

name: Carafa Special II (De-husked)
description: Medium-dark de-husked roasted malt providing deep ebony color, dark chocolate, and roasted hazelnut with ultra-smooth drinkability.
typicalUsage: 1–5% in Schwarzbier, Baltic Porters, and Black IPAs.

name: Blackprinz Malt
description: De-husked hull-less black barley malt from Briess. Yields intense black color with almost no roasted bitterness or astringency, perfect for smooth dark beers.
typicalUsage: 1–5% for color adjustment in Black IPAs, Stouts, and Porters.

name: Torrefied Wheat
description: Heat-puffed raw wheat grains that require no pre-cooking. Greatly improves head retention, foam density, and body in traditional British ales.
typicalUsage: 5–15% in British Bitters, IPAs, and Milds for head retention.

name: Malted Oats
description: Fully malted whole oat grain with intact husks. Provides silky smooth body and stable haze without the lautering stickiness of flaked oats, thanks to the filtering husks.
typicalUsage: 10–30% in New England/Hazy IPAs, Oatmeal Stouts, and Farmhouse ales.

name: Golden Naked Oats (Crystal Oat Malt)
description: De-husked oat kernels stewed and crystal-roasted by Simpsons. Delivers intense toasted nutty, creamy toffee, and toasted oatmeal sweetness with lush body.
typicalUsage: 5–15% in Hazy IPAs, English Bitters, Stouts, and Brown Ales.

name: Chocolate Rye Malt
description: Drum-roasted rye grain from Weyermann. Combines rich roasted coffee and dark cocoa with the spicy, peppery, pumpernickel bite of rye.
typicalUsage: 1–5% in Roggenbier, Dark Lagers, Stouts, and Rye Porters.

name: Peated Distilling Malt
description: Barley malt kilned over smoking Scottish peat bogs. Infuses potent medicinal, smoky, phenolic, earthy iodine notes. Must be used with great caution in brewing.
typicalUsage: 0.5–3% in Scottish Wee Heavies, Smoked Porters, and experimental beers.
